t: For an additional amount for “Department of Health and Human Services, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Disease Control, Research and Training”, to carry out section 501 of the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act of 1977, $10,000,000 for research to develop mine safety technology: Provided, That progress reports on technology development shall be submitted to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations and the Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Education and the Workforce of the House on a quarterly basis, with the first report due July 15, 2006: Provided further, That the amount provided under this heading shall remain available until September 30, 2007: Provided further, That the amount provided under this heading is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 402 of H. Con. Res. 95 (109th Congress), the concurrent resolution on the budget for fiscal year 2006.

fable.w: This is an appropriation for mine safety research with a requirement to send quarterly progress reports to congressional committees. The tempting reading is that the reporting requirement is a form of consultation, but Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so no outside party is involved in any federal decision. Nothing in the section provides for public comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or consultation with states or other outside entities.
fable.s: progress reports on technology development shall be submitted to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations and the Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Education and the Workforce of the House on a quarterly basis

qwen_block.w: This section requires the submission of progress reports to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for consultation with states, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: progress reports on technology development shall be submitted to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations and the Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Education and the Workforce of the House

opus.w: This section funds mine safety research and requires progress reports to congressional committees. It might look like participation because there is a required formal reporting process, but Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, so the reports never reach anyone outside it. Nothing here calls for a comment period, a public hearing, an outside advisory body, consultation with states or other outside parties, or a right to sue.
opus.s: progress reports on technology development shall be submitted to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations and the Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Education and the Workforce of the House on a quarterly basis

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the submission of progress reports to various congressional committees. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are considered inside the federal government. Therefore, this reporting requirement is an intra-governmental action and does not involve consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: progress reports on technology development shall be submitted to the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations and the Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Education and the Workforce of the House on a quarterly basis
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that requiring progress reports to congressional committees constitutes "participation" because it involves external oversight. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, reporting to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation by outside parties.
